# Harvard Guide to Using Sources

> A comprehensive resource for Harvard students on evaluating, locating, integrating, and citing sources across MLA, APA, and Chicago styles while maintaining academic integrity.

This guide serves Harvard College students and the broader academic community with practical instruction on research methodology, source evaluation, citation management, and plagiarism prevention. It covers discipline-specific source usage and provides tools for effective scholarly communication.

## Key Topics

- Citation styles (MLA, APA, Chicago)
- Academic integrity
- Plagiarism prevention
- Source evaluation
- Source integration
- Harvard libraries and HOLLIS
- Citation management tools (Zotero, Endnote)
- Research methodology
- Primary and secondary sources
- College writing standards
- Chicago Manual of Style
- Common knowledge exception
- Harvard College Honor Code
- Source attribution
- Scholarly research practices

## Citation Formats & Reference

- [Citing Sources](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/citing-sources-0): Overview of MLA, APA, and Chicago citation formats and source attribution
- [MLA](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/mla-0): Complete MLA style guide with works-cited formatting and source documentation
- [APA](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/apa-0): Complete APA style guide with in-text citations and reference formatting
- [Chicago](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/chicago-0): Chicago Manual of Style and Turabian guide with footnotes, bibliography, and examples
- [Citation Management Tools](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/citation-management-tools): Guide to Zotero, Endnote, and Overleaf Pro for source organization and citation

## Academic Integrity & Plagiarism

- [Avoiding Plagiarism](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/avoiding-plagiarism-0): Guide to academic integrity, citation standards, and Harvard College Honor Code
- [What Constitutes Plagiarism?](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/what-constitutes-plagiarism-0): Defines plagiarism types, verbatim plagiarism, and web source citation requirements
- [How to Avoid Plagiarism](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/how-avoid-plagiarism-0): Best practices for source management, citation, and plagiarism prevention strategies
- [The Exception: Common Knowledge](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/exception-common-knowledge-0): Explains common knowledge exception to citation requirements in academic writing
- [Why Does it Matter if You Plagiarize?](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/why-does-it-matter-if-you-plagiarize-0): Explains plagiarism consequences, honor code, and scholarly standards at Harvard
- [Other Scenarios to Avoid](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/other-scenarios-avoid-0): Guide to avoiding source misrepresentation and citation ethics violations

## Research & Source Skills

- [Using Sources](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/using-sources-0): Overview of evaluating, integrating, and using Harvard library sources for research
- [Locating Sources](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/locating-sources-0): Guide to locating and selecting sources using Harvard libraries and research process
- [Evaluating Sources](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/evaluating-sources-0): How to evaluate source reliability, peer-reviewed journals, and credibility
- [Integrating Sources](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/integrating-sources-0): Guide to integrating sources into papers with proper citation and paper structure
- [Why Use Sources?](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/why-use-sources-0): Guide explaining primary and secondary sources and field-specific source types

## Writing & Academic Papers

- [What Are You Supposed to Do with Sources?](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/what-are-you-supposed-do-sources-0): Tutorial on using sources for analysis, argumentation, and research papers
- [Writing "Original" Papers](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/writing-original-papers-0): Guide to developing original thesis and meeting instructor expectations for college papers
- [Using Sources Beyond Harvard](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu/using-sources-beyond-harvard): Guide to source usage across disciplines: business, legal, medical, and professional writing

## Getting Started

- [Harvard Guide to Using Sources](https://usingsources.fas.harvard.edu): Harvard's comprehensive guide to using sources, citing in MLA, APA, and Chicago styles
